lead.headline: Chasing Glory Put Up The Biggest Score In Cartel History, And It Still Only Counts Once
lead.dek: 237.88 from Raptor on Sunday, more than any team has managed in four seasons of this league, and more than the two clubs in the week's other game scored between them. He clinched with it. He's seventh on the dynasty board and owns 0.36 points of draft capital, so there isn't a second act.
body: THE CARTEL — Here's the number, and then here's why it's strange. Chasing Glory scored 237.88 against Hoya Paranoia on Sunday. Nobody in Dynasty Cartel has ever scored that much in a week. The old mark was 231.12, set by 100 Yards And Runnin in Week 9 of last season, and before Sunday it had stood for a year.

Jahmyr Gibbs went 44.70. Dak Prescott went 41.42 out of the superflex and George Pickens 40.00 and Brock Purdy 36.66, and James Cook added 23.70 in a week where Raptor could have left him out and still won by sixty. The roster was worth 261.98 and he converted 90.8 percent of it. That's a very good afternoon on top of an extraordinary one.

Now the strange part. Blame spanos scored 208.34 in the same hour, the seventh-biggest week this league has on file, and beat Too High Safeties by 167.74 — the widest margin in four years of Cartel football. Meanwhile Lovely Day beat Trade Calculator Guy 77.88 to 68.86. Add those two together and you get 146.74. Raptor beat that by himself, with 91.14 to spare.

So Week 10 holds the league record for points and the league record for margin on the same card, and it also holds a game neither side could drag to eighty. That's not a scoring week. That's a league coming apart into two different leagues, and the odds have caught up with it.

Raptor has clinched. So has Cheddar Bobs, who's 8-2 and beat 100 Yards And Runnin by twenty. Four clubs are now mathematically finished — Out. Of. Town. Shooters., Somewhat Goodfellas, Lovely Day and Too High Safeties, the last of them 0-10 and 100 percent certain to pick last. Four more sit between 97.9 and 98.9 percent. Exactly one team in this league still has a live question attached to it, and that team is 100 Yards And Runnin at 6.4 percent, down from 28.6 a week ago.

What Raptor cannot do is press the advantage. The dynasty board puts Chasing Glory seventh of twelve at 30.45, and only 0.36 of that is draft picks — the smallest holding in the league by a distance, because he spent it in Week 6 on Travis Kelce, DJ Moore and James Cook. Four weeks on, that deal looks like the best piece of business of the season: Cook and Moore gave him 41.10 of Sunday's total, and the four-week review on this page files it A- against a D. The bill is that there's nothing left to buy with.

And the hole is visible even inside 237.88. Chasing Glory is first in the league at quarterback with 435.02 points and first at running back with 542.80, and ninth at receiver with 291.10. Pickens went for forty on Sunday and the two receivers beside him managed 21.00 between them, one of those Tank Dell on 3.60 with Ryan Flournoy's 16.10 sitting on the bench. A team that scores the most points ever and is ninth of twelve at a starting position has not fixed anything. It has had a Sunday.

The counter-argument is the one Greg Olsen makes on the Power Rankings page, and it's fair: you win a title with the best three weeks of December, not the best average of September through November, and nobody in this league has shown a three-week ceiling like this one. Raptor's form figure is 182.11 a week, highest in the Cartel. His title probability is 37.8 percent, nearly double the next man's. On the simulations he's the best team here by a wide margin and the record just said so out loud.

The paper's own position, for the record, is that the receiver room is the thing that beats him and the deadline is Week 14. Weeks 11 through 14, and then the trade window shuts for the year. He has $0 of FAAB and 0.36 of picks, and the only currency he has is a running back room four deep in a league where eleven other managers can all read the same table.

notebook.title: Football Morning in the Cartel
intro: I spent Sunday evening with a spreadsheet open and a pot of coffee I shouldn't have made at six o'clock, trying to work out whether 237.88 was the biggest number this league had ever produced. It is. Four seasons of this league and it took until Sunday, and it landed on an afternoon when somebody else in the same league couldn't find eighty points with ten starters and a waiver claim.

That's the thing I can't get past. The Cartel's record score and the Cartel's record margin landed inside the same four hours. So did the lowest score anybody has filed this season. Twelve managers, one Sunday, and the gap between the top of it and the bottom of it was 197.28 points.

ten_things: 1. The playoff field is now a formality and the arithmetic says so plainly. Chasing Glory and Cheddar Bobs have clinched. Blame spanos is 98.9 percent, COME AND TAKE IT 98.6, Not F*cking Around Crew 98.2 and Hoya Paranoia 97.9. Four clubs are at zero. That's eleven of twelve settled, and the twelfth is 100 Yards And Runnin at 6.4 percent.

2. I want to be careful with the word collapse, because barringinjury is the sixth-highest scorer in this league at 141.71 a week and his lineup would be the second-best in the Cartel on the valuation desk's own rate table. What's happened to him isn't performance. He's 71-39 against the whole field and 4-6 against the schedule, and that minus 2.45 luck figure is the largest in the league in either direction.

3. He started three tight ends on Sunday. Darren Waller at the position, Brock Bowers and George Kittle in the two flex slots, 21.60 between them. That's not a mistake in a tight-end premium league where he's first at the position and ninth at running back — it's the only lineup he has. It also means the two most valuable pieces he owns are competing with each other for one slot that matters.

4. Three teams started three tight ends, in fact. Eight tight ends were filed in flex slots across twelve lineups, and five of them scored under five points. The premium is doing something strange to this league and I don't think anybody has solved it yet.

5. Nobody in the Cartel filed a man the NFL had already ruled out of the game. Second straight week of that. T.J. Hockenson was Out by Friday and eloper pulled him for Noah Gray, which is the single thing I'd point to if somebody asked me whether a fantasy newspaper does anything useful at all.

6. The waiver economy has broken down and the numbers are brutal. Eighty claims this season, $970 spent, and the grader records zero hits. One useful pickup. Six fillers. Twenty men claimed, never started and released. Thirty-five still being stashed. The best claim of the year remains tdsmith23's $58 on Emanuel Wilson in Week 3, worth +22.04 above replacement in three starts, and he's the same manager who's burned $94 on two men he cut inside a month.

7. Somewhat Goodfellas has not spent a dollar. Not one, all season, out of $200. eloper is 4-6, eliminated, converting 89.1 percent of a roster that averages 110.95, and ten weeks of free-agent windows have gone by without him testing a single one.

8. Four clubs are out of money entirely — Chasing Glory, COME AND TAKE IT, 100 Yards And Runnin and the Crew — and three of them have clinched or are above 98 percent. So the six teams going to the playoffs hold $426 of FAAB between them and the six that aren't hold $401. That's the deadline problem in one line: the sellers have the cash and the buyers have the need.

9. Somebody should tell Too High Safeties that his own 2027 first-round pick isn't his. He's 0-10, he's locked into twelfth, and the pick that comes out of it goes to the Crew, who bought it in 2024. The two 2027 firsts DavisNuaimi does hold belong to Cheddar Bobs and the Crew, who are 8-2 and 7-3. He is going to finish last and draft in the twenties.

10. A number I keep turning over: 20.7 percent of all the value on the dynasty board sits on players this league has started twice or fewer. Roy Cowgirl writes about this on the Dynasty page and he's right to. A fifth of what we're all arguing about is a guess the model made about men nobody here has watched play.

Raptor goes to first, TJWill drops to second after winning, and rkobeb2000 climbs two. That's it at the sharp end. Underneath that, four teams are out and the shape of the back half of this season is set.

He's 80-30 against the whole field. His luck's basically flat at minus 0.27. He's just good, and on Sunday he was better than anybody in this league's ever been. What I'd say is this: he's ninth at receiver and he's got no money and no picks. That's a real thing in December, and he knows it.

rumors.title: Charles Robinson's Notebook
rumors.byline: Charles Robinson · Not F*cking Around Crew, roster 11
rumors.standing: Standing disclaimer: none of this is reporting. Nobody quoted here has said a word to me, every trade below is invented, and I'm in the standings — I hold five of the twelve 2027 firsts, I'm first on the dynasty board by 14.92, and on Sunday I won by 1.52 with 32.02 points of my own roster sitting on the bench. One of the deals below is a deal I'd make myself. I've flagged it. Read accordingly.
lede: The useful thing about Week 10 isn't the record. It's that the market just resolved. A week ago there were seven clubs who could tell themselves a story about January. Now there are six, plus one man at 6.4 percent who has to decide this week which side of the line he's on.

So for the first time this season you can say with a straight face who the buyers are and who the sellers are, and the prices follow from that. Here's the awkward part for everybody holding something worth having: the six buyers have $426 of FAAB between them and three of them have none at all. I'm one of the three. The sellers are sitting on $401 they no longer need.
That means the deadline won't be settled in cash. It gets settled in picks and in players, which is the market I like, and it's the market I've spent two years getting ready for.

items.head: At 6.4 percent, the best tight end room in the league belongs to a man who can't use it
body: 100 Yards And Runnin has 259.70 points at tight end in ten weeks, first in the Cartel by 63.80. He also started three of them on Sunday — Waller at the slot, Bowers and Kittle in both flexes — for 21.60 between them, because he's ninth at running back and there was nothing else to file. That's a roster telling its manager something.

What I'm told about barringinjury, which is nothing, because nobody tells me anything, is beside the point here. The numbers do it. He's the sixth-best scorer in this league, 71-39 against the field, minus 2.45 on luck, and 6.4 percent to play a playoff game. Seven days ago he was at 28.6. He can hold two elite tight ends for a division he's not winning, or he can turn one of them into the running back room he's actually short of.
And both of his tight ends have a buyer. Cheddar Bobs is 8-2, clinched, and dead last in this league at the position with 57.00 points. Here's the deal that works on my table.

deal.label: The deal that makes sense
deal.verdict: Dead level on the desk's table and both starting elevens get better, which is rare. Cheddar Bobs gains 2.97 points a week by replacing Mike Gesicki's slot with the best tight end in the deal, and he's selling from the position he's second in. 100 Yards And Runnin gains 0.32 by widening a receiver room that went Jefferson, Nabers and Vele on Sunday for 19.20. It's the sort of trade two managers do in ten minutes if either of them picks up the phone.

items.fit: Bowers prices at 3.85 and Evans, Meyers and Ewers at 3.84 together, so the tilt is a tenth of one percent. Cheddar Bobs starts Gesicki at 1.90 and Hunter Henry at 4.20 in a flex, and the position has cost him 57.00 points in ten weeks against a league average of 144.66. He's got $150 of FAAB and nothing on the wire to spend it on, so this has to be a trade.

items.head: The other tight end has a second buyer, and the second buyer is me
body: I'm going to be careful here, because this is the item where I'm the interested party. I started Sam LaPorta at tight end on Sunday for 2.60. Colston Loveland and Kenyon Sadiq are both on my roster and both are 22 or younger and neither has done anything yet. I'm seventh in the Cartel at the position with 142.20 and I'm 7-3.

George Kittle costs less than Bowers because he's 32 and the model ages him hard. He's priced at 1.93 against Bowers' 3.85, and for a club that's trying to win this year rather than hold value, that discount is the whole trade. Here's what I'd actually pay.

And I'd pay it in a 2029 first rather than a 2027 one, because the 2027 firsts I own are the point of my entire roster and I'm not breaking the set for a tight end. If barringinjury wants a 2027 first out of this league he should call deucebrat, who took his off him in Week 8 for D'Andre Swift and Darren Waller.

deal.label: The deal I'd make myself
deal.verdict: A percent apart on the table and both lineups improve. I gain 2.52 a week putting Kittle in LaPorta's slot, which is the largest single fix available to me without selling a back. He gains 0.52 and a first-round pick three years out, which for a 4-6 team with no budget is the right shape of payment. If he does this one and the Bowers deal above, he's got no tight end left and he loses 3.76 a week doing it. At 6.4 percent I'd argue that's exactly what he should want.

items.fit: Kittle prices at 1.93. Odunze at 0.93 plus a 2029 first at 0.96 makes 1.89, so the deal tilts 1.1 percent my way. I have two 2029 firsts and three 2028 firsts and five 2027 firsts, and I've got $0 of FAAB, so paper is the only thing I can pay with. Odunze is 24 and he scored nothing for me on Sunday.

items.head: Chasing Glory scored 237.88 and is still ninth at receiver, and he's got nothing to pay with
body: Two hundred and thirty-seven points and his receivers went 61.00. Pickens had forty of it. That's not a criticism of a league record, it's a description of a roster: first at quarterback, first at running back, ninth at receiver, $0 of FAAB and 0.36 points of draft capital. The whole future is in the lineup already.

So he pays from the back room or he doesn't pay. Gibbs, Cook, Jaylen Warren and Kenny Gainwell is four deep, and on Sunday Warren took one flex slot for 6.60 while Blake Corum had the other for 21.40. Tyler Warren started at tight end for 2.40 with Travis Kelce on the bench, which tells you how he rates the pair of them.

Trade Calculator Guy is the natural counterparty and the one nobody wants to call, because igross has spent the season buying and has a 3-7 record to show for it. But he's rebuilding now whether he likes it or not, and a 30-year-old receiver is no use to him.

deal.label: The deal neither of them will call about
deal.verdict: Two tenths of a percent apart. Chasing Glory gains 1.67 a week, which is the only receiver fix on the board that doesn't cost him Gibbs or Cook. igross drops 1.98 a week and gets a 24-year-old tight end for a 30-year-old receiver, which is the trade a 3-7 club is supposed to want. He'd rather have a pick, and Raptor hasn't got one to give, and that's why this doesn't happen.

items.fit: Sutton 1.86 and Benson 0.48 against Tyler Warren 1.75 and Doubs 0.60. Chasing Glory's whole draft holding prices at 0.36, which is one 2028 third and four 2028 fourths and a pair of 2029s, so a first-round pick isn't available to him at any price. Kelce covers the tight end slot he'd be vacating.

items.head: The 0-10 team is not the worst roster in this league, and that matters for what he can get
body: Too High Safeties lost by 167.74 and scored 40.60, and I want to push back on the obvious reading of that. He converted 88.5 percent of his ceiling. His ceiling was 45.90. The lineup card was fine and there was simply nothing in it.

But the board has him tenth rather than last, 179.50 points at tight end puts him third in the league at the position, and 40.4 percent of his price sits on men this league has started twice or fewer. That last figure is the one to handle carefully. It isn't that he's rich. It's that nobody actually knows what he has.

The thing I'd pump the brakes on is the idea that he should be selling. He owns two 2027 firsts and both belong to playoff teams, so they'll land late. His own first, the one that comes out of 0-10, belongs to me. A club in that position doesn't sell. It buys the cheapest young thing it can find and waits, and it should be bidding its remaining $16 on every rookie that clears waivers between now and Week 14.
items.fit: 179.50 at tight end against a league-low 57.00 and a league-high 259.70. Dynasty board: 19.93 total, 11.99 in players and 7.94 in picks, 0.0 percent of his assets clearing replacement level on current rate. The 2027 firsts he holds are Cheddar Bobs' and mine, and we're 8-2 and 7-3.

heard: Out. Of. Town. Shooters. released Ashton Dulin on 11 November to make room for a $10 claim on Cole Payton, then reclaimed Dulin for nothing on 14 November. Payton himself had been dropped by igross three days earlier to fit the $179 Kyle McCord claim. Three managers, one week, four transactions, and the net effect is that everybody ended up roughly where they started.

The waiver grader has recorded zero hits across 80 claims and $970 this season. Not one pickup in this league has returned eight points a start above replacement. Twenty claims were never started and then released, and $166 of real money went with them.

Somewhat Goodfellas still holds all $200. eloper is eliminated and he's first in the Cartel at receiver, which makes him the one seller with both an asset and the budget to not care. Jaxon Smith-Njigba prices at 5.92, the fourth-highest number on the desk's table, and there are four clubs who could use him and none who can pay the freight in cash.

COME AND TAKE IT owns nothing in any future draft. Not a first, not a fourth, nothing across the next three classes. He's 7-3 and 98.6 percent to qualify, and the only route to a better roster before Week 14 runs through trading a starter for a starter. I've been staring at that board for three weeks and I don't see the deal.

Lovely Day holds two 2027 firsts — his own, and the one he took off 100 Yards And Runnin in Week 8 for D'Andre Swift and Darren Waller. Seven days ago that acquired pick belonged to a club at 28.6 percent. It now belongs to a club at 6.4. deucebrat has had the best week of anybody in this league without beating anybody good.

signoff.label: Last word

On Sunday I started Drake Maye for 3.02 with Cam Ward scoring 21.14 on the bench and won by 1.52. The roster is the best thing in this league and the lineup card is the worst thing about me, and in a bracket you only get to be wrong about that once.

Chasing Glory's purchase of Kelce, DJ Moore and James Cook grades A- against a D, and Hoya Paranoia's buy of Amon-Ra St. Brown grades A- against a D as well. dynasty_column.byline: By Roy Cowgirl · A current NFL broadcaster · Name withheld at the writer's request
intro: The board didn't move this week. Not a cent. Charles Robinson is still first at 64.15, Hoya Paranoia second at 49.23, 100 Yards And Runnin third at 45.65, and the order runs the same as it did seven days ago. That's because the prices are frozen at Week 4 and only get rebuilt when the collector runs. I'd rather tell you that than let you think I recalculated something.

What did move is the thing underneath. Chasing Glory scored more points on Sunday than anybody in this league ever has, and he's seventh here. That's the widest gap between the two boards — first on power, seventh on dynasty, six places — and it isn't a mistake in either table. He's got 30.09 in players and 0.36 in picks. He's renting a contender. He's done it on purpose and it's working.

Robinson's the reverse and I'll say it plainly even though he writes in this paper. Seventh on power, first here, 64.15 against a league average of 33.16. Fourteen and a half clear of second. He owns five of twelve 2027 firsts. And he's got 19.3 percent of his price clearing replacement level on current form, which means four-fifths of what he's holding is a bet on later.

Here's where my own table is soft, because somebody has to say it. Twenty point seven percent of all the value on this board rests on players this league has started twice or fewer. A fifth. The model's most confident numbers are its least evidenced ones, and that's not a bug I can fix — it's what happens when you price a 22-year-old off a curve instead of off tape.

The worst of it is Somewhat Goodfellas at 49.3 percent thin. Half of what eloper is credited with is men nobody here has watched play. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is 45.2 percent, Too High Safeties 40.4. All three are eliminated. Read those three totals as a range, not a number.

And the cleanest number on the board belongs to the man at the bottom. Lovely Day is twelfth at 16.40 and only 7.2 percent of it is thin — the lowest share in the league. There's no hidden upside in deucebrat's roster. What you see is what he's got, and what he's got is 10.66 in players and two 2027 firsts.

Four clubs show 0.0 percent startable: Lovely Day, Too High Safeties, Trade Calculator Guy and the Shooters. That's not a bug either. I checked it in Week 7 when it first appeared and I'll give the same answer now — every priced man on those four rosters sits below this league's replacement level on rate. They've won ten games between them and lost thirty, and all four are eliminated, so for once the board and the standings are telling the same story.

My partner spent the whole second quarter on Sunday explaining why a team that scores the most points is the best team. Took him eleven minutes. The board's been saying it for a month and it fits on one line.

draft_column.byline: By Mel Kiper Jr. · The Draft Room
intro: Ten weeks of 2026 football are on the board and I've regraded all 432 selections this league has ever made — 240 in the 2023 startup, 48 each in the 2023 rookie draft and in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The grade is what the pick has put into a starting lineup. It is not my opinion from draft night and it is not what a trade calculator says this morning.

Same order, different numbers. Every manager gained somewhere between 1.1 and 6.8 a selection this week, because the denominator sits still while the football keeps arriving. Chasing Glory holds first at 287.5 a pick from TWENTY picks — twenty! — which is 53.7 ahead of second. Twenty selections against thirty-nine for the manager at the foot of the page, and better than twice the per-pick return. Call that scouting, because variance doesn't look like that.

Here's what I want on the record. The thousand-point club has seven members now and Christian McCaffrey joined it on Sunday with 48.30 — he went 2.19 of the startup, nineteenth overall, and TJWill has never let go of him. Four of the seven are quarterbacks. Three of the seven have been traded at least once, and all three of those were taken in the first two rounds of the 2023 startup or the first round of the rookie draft that followed it. The best selections in league history mostly didn't stay home.

board.head: Six first-round picks have never scored a point and four of them came last April
board.body: From 2026: Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08, Ty Simpson at 1.09, Eli Stowers at 1.10 and Omar Cooper at 1.11. Two are older. Travis Hunter went 1.03 in 2025 and Sleeper lists him at defensive back, which means he will never register a single point for anybody here. Kaleb Johnson went 1.09 the same April and has simply produced nothing. Hunter belongs to Hoya Paranoia and Johnson to Trade Calculator Guy, and both managers have had eighteen months to make peace with it.

board.head: The two best tight end selections in league history went in the eighth and twelfth rounds, and neither man kept his
board.body: Trey McBride, round 12 of the 2023 startup to Out. Of. Town. Shooters., 668.20 points, now Hoya Paranoia's. George Kittle, round 8 of the same draft to Hoya Paranoia, 661.90 points, now 100 Yards And Runnin's. Brock Bowers at 1.08 of 2024 is third at 505.50 and is the only one of the three still with the manager who called the name. In a league that pays a tight end premium, the two most productive ones at the position cost a combined twentieth-round equivalent.

board.head: The fifth round of the startup beats the fourth, the eighth beats the seventh, and the eleventh is worse than the twentieth
board.body: The 2023 startup pays 879.5 a pick in round one, 663.6 in round two and 511.5 in round three. After that the pattern falls apart. Round four averages 397.0 and round five 436.5. Round six collapses to 208.8, round seven recovers to 331.2 and round eight to 391.4. Round eleven pays 82.7, round twelve 210.3, and round eighteen 176.8 — so the eleventh round of this draft was worse than the eighteenth. Twelve managers ranked two hundred and forty players, and the ranking held up for three rounds.

sunday.title: Sunday Brief
sunday.byline: Filed Sunday morning, before the one o'clock kickoffs
lede: Not one bye-week starter anywhere this morning. Four clubs are idle — Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay — and all 45 of their players held in this league are sitting on benches where they belong. No empty slots either, and nobody has left a man on IR in a lineup. Fix This First is blank.

One slot is broken, and it's a tight end. Somewhat Goodfellas has T.J. Hockenson filed at tight end, and Minnesota ruled him out with a wrist — he didn't practice on any of the three days. That's a 0.00 in the slot eloper can least afford, because he's eleventh of twelve in tight end scoring and Hockenson is the only reason it isn't worse: 12 of 17 targets caught for 126 yards and a pair of touchdowns since Week 7. Noah Gray is on his bench on six catches from six targets, 70 yards and a score across the same three games, and he carries no designation. Eli Stowers is on Philadelphia's bye and Joe Royer hasn't played a down. Two hours left, one click.

calls.head: Chasing Glory put Tank Dell in for Tre Tucker, and this is the game you don't guess in
calls.body: Raptor against jlundblad is the closest pairing on the board and it isn't close to being close: 146.62 of three-week form against 146.41, a gap of 0.21 where the next tightest game is 2.88 apart. The overnight card had Tre Tucker in the third receiver slot. The live one has Tank Dell, who's played two games since coming back and taken five catches on ten targets for 148 yards and a score in them, practiced in full all week and carries no designation. Tucker has 33 catches on 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns on the season, and 11.78 a start across six starts here. Dell is the better two-game bet and Tucker is the better nine-game one. Chasing Glory is tenth of twelve at receiver, so there's no third option to hide behind. In a game decided by a fifth of a point of form, take the nine games. The flex pair is fine as filed — Blake Corum has 39 carries for 224 yards and three scores over three weeks and shouldn't move.

calls.head: Hoya Paranoia has a back who has never started for him in the second running back slot
calls.body: Lan Larison is in at running back with three carries for ten yards to his name all season and not one start in this league. Emanuel Wilson is on the bench on 111 carries for 403 yards and three touchdowns, 24 of those carries and 100 of those yards inside the last three weeks, and 16.23 a start across four starts here. Nothing about the designations explains it: neither man is on this week's report. What does explain the thin bench is the calendar — the byes took Saquon Barkley, Bucky Irving, Jaylen Waddle and Caleb Williams out of that room in one week, and David Montgomery is questionable with a groin behind them. It's the same 0.21 game, and this is the slot in it that's actually fixable.

calls.head: Cheddar Bobs took Kenneth Walker out this morning, and the inactive list hasn't landed yet
calls.body: Walker is the best back in this league by the only measure that pays: 26.14 points a start over seven starts, ahead of Jahmyr Gibbs at 25.77 and everybody else by five. He's also questionable with a groin and didn't practice on any day, and over the last three weeks he's still gone 53 carries for 207 yards and a score, plus 12 catches on 14 targets for 77 more. The overnight card had him at running back. The live one has Chase Brown there at 9.97 a start and Jakobi Meyers in a flex on one start and 10.8. TJWill is 7-2 and drawing barringinjury, the second-tightest game of the week at 2.88 of form. The inactives post ninety minutes before kickoff. If Walker dresses, Meyers is the slot to hand back, and nobody should be touching this one before then.

calls.head: Braelon Allen's 46 carries are on the Crew's bench in a three-point game
calls.body: Not F*cking Around Crew against BADS is 136.89 against 140.54, third-closest this week, and both flex slots are filled by men the last month hasn't backed. Quinshon Judkins has 43 carries for 164 yards and two touchdowns over three weeks and 5.75 a start here. Jalen Coker has seven catches on 14 targets for 74 yards and a score, and 5.63 a start. Braelon Allen, benched, has 46 carries for 284 yards and a touchdown over the same three weeks plus ten catches on 11 targets, and 14.90 a start across four. Judkins has the touchdowns and an argument. Coker is the slot to change, and the tight-end trick that covered this last week isn't available — Colston Loveland is on Chicago's bye.

wire.line: Unrostered, and he's taken six catches on 11 targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in two games over the last three weeks. Trade Calculator Guy is the fit: Jordan Addison is questionable with a thumb and has returned 4.97 a start over seven of them.

Six catches from six targets, 81 yards since Week 7, and nothing on the injury report. Tight end catches carry extra weight in this format, so he belongs on one of the three thinnest rooms at the position — Cheddar Bobs is last of twelve, Somewhat Goodfellas eleventh, Blame spanos tenth.
Three catches on four targets for 92 yards and a score in two games. Same shelf as Evans and the bigger play per touch, if you'd rather bet on the yards than the volume.
Four catches on four targets for 109 yards in two games. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is twelfth of twelve at receiver and already starts Tyler Shough, so the stack is free.

Worth saying plainly, because Somewhat Goodfellas is twelfth of twelve there and needs one: the most-used unrostered back of the last three weeks is Tyler Goodson, and he's out with an ankle. After him it's Ameer Abdullah on 13 carries for 43 yards. The wire can't fix a backfield today.

watch: A.J. Brown is in the COME AND TAKE IT superflex on 4.87 a start, questionable with an ankle and limited all week — and the quarterback room behind him is gone, with Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels on byes and Kyler Murray out with a hamstring. Cooper Kupp is the fallback if Brown is inactive.

The rib has Amon-Ra St. Brown listed questionable, and he was limited on all three practice days. Since Week 7 he's caught 24 of 29 targets for 285 yards. Keenan Allen, on 14 of 18 for 124, is the only receiver behind him on that bench without a designation of his own.
Garrett Wilson is questionable with a concussion but practiced in full every day, which usually means he plays. Watch him dress rather than plan around him.

Four of Trade Calculator Guy's six quarterbacks are off this week — Jalen Hurts, Bo Nix, Tanner McKee and Jarrett Stidham. That's how a receiver with 2.00 points in his only start ends up in a superflex slot.

Too High Safeties has Denzel Boston questionable with a toe and Jalen Milroe, who has never started, in the superflex. At 0-9 against the league's hottest team it won't decide anything, but the slots are still empty of points.
sunday.signoff: One Out tag to clear, two hours to clear it, and the rest of you are already in good order — go watch the games.

initial.verdict: Chasing Glory buys back its own 2027 first for Marvin Harrison, a 24-year-old the Crew had just acquired and flipped in three weeks. Getting your own pick back is rarely a bad outcome; paying a young No. 1 receiver for it is the part that will age.

4wk.verdict: Four weeks on, the pick has not been used and Marvin Harrison has not started a game for Not F*cking Around Crew. Chasing Glory is now 95.3% to qualify, so the first-rounder it bought back is heading for the twenties — and the Crew paid for that privilege with a 24-year-old receiver it keeps behind five others.

initial.verdict: The defining deal of the offseason. Somewhat Goodfellas collected three 2028 firsts, a 2027 third and Jordan Addison for one running back. Blame spanos got the best pure runner in the league at 24 and no 2028 draft to fall back on.

4wk.verdict: Bijan Robinson has returned 93.70 points above replacement in five starts for Blame spanos, the largest figure attached to any deal in this league's 2026 book. Somewhat Goodfellas paid with Jordan Addison, three 2028 first-round picks and a third, then moved Addison on inside a month; the picks are the entire case for his side and none of them can be graded before 2028.

initial.verdict: A one-way move of a fifth-round-profile rookie receiver. Small enough that the only real cost is roster space.

4wk.verdict: Nothing to grade and nothing coming. Chimere Dike has not started for Chasing Glory and the other side of the ledger is empty in the file. After four weeks this remains a roster-trimming exercise that happened to be filed as a trade.

initial.verdict: A 2029 third for a 2029 second, three years out. Both sides are trading paper nobody can value yet.

4wk.verdict: A 2029 second against a 2029 third, with three seasons to run before either becomes a name. Not F*cking Around Crew holds the better end on the valuation desk's pick table and will not find out for a very long time whether that mattered.

initial.verdict: Age for age: Mark Andrews at 31 and a rookie receiver, against Xavier Worthy at 23 and a developmental wideout. Hoya Paranoia took the younger half of a dynasty trade, which is usually the right half.

4wk.verdict: Mark Andrews has made three starts for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and finished 4.60 points below what a free agent at the position was returning. Xavier Worthy has not started for Hoya Paranoia at all. Both sides are underwater and neither has beaten the waiver wire, which the model records as no gain rather than a narrow win.

initial.verdict: Out. Of. Town. Shooters. turned DK Metcalf and a 2029 first into Jaylen Waddle — younger, cheaper, and a first-round pick lighter for the other side. Waddle then opened the season with 0.7 points.

4wk.verdict: The closest thing to a dead heat in this release: Jaylen Waddle 7.50 above replacement in five starts, DK Metcalf 6.90 in five. Blame spanos also holds a 2029 first for his trouble, which is the only thing separating them, and Metcalf gave him 3.80 on Sunday.

initial.verdict: COME AND TAKE IT paid a 29-year-old receiver's price for Rachaad White and a depth wideout. The volume is real; the upside is not.

4wk.verdict: Neither roster has started anybody it received. DK Metcalf left Out. Of. Town. Shooters. again before he could play a game for them, and Rachaad White and Jalen McMillan have not made COME AND TAKE IT's ten. Four weeks of nothing on both sides.

initial.verdict: Mooney and Matthew Golden for a rookie and pick swaps. Somewhat Goodfellas gets usable receivers now without giving up anything that matters in 2028.

4wk.verdict: 36.10 points above replacement in five starts for Somewhat Goodfellas, most of it Matthew Golden, who scored 19.30 on Sunday. Hoya Paranoia holds a 2027 third and a rookie receiver who has not dressed. It is the best trade Somewhat Goodfellas has made and he is 0.5% to reach January.

initial.verdict: Too High Safeties turns a rookie receiver into three bodies. When you are 9-33 lifetime, quantity is not the answer.

4wk.verdict: Three bodies for one and not a start between them. Ted Hurst sits on the Crew's taxi squad; two of the three men who went the other way are still on Too High Safeties' roster and none has played. A depth shuffle, correctly graded as nothing.

initial.verdict: A pick-for-pick tidy-up with nothing on either side worth a paragraph.

4wk.verdict: Both sides of this one are empty in the file — no players, no picks recorded against either roster. There is nothing to grade now and there will not be anything later.

initial.verdict: Lovely Day sold A.J. Brown at 29 for D'Andre Swift, Ricky Pearsall and a 2029 third. Swift went for 33.9 in Week 1 and was the only reason Lovely Day survived its nine-man lineup.

4wk.verdict: 47.30 points above replacement in five starts for Lovely Day, nearly all of it D'Andre Swift, who has started every week and scored 15.30 on Sunday. A.J. Brown has started once for COME AND TAKE IT, finished 2.80 below replacement, and is now on its injured reserve. The proprietor of this newspaper won a trade.

initial.verdict: Two future fourths for one 2026 fourth. Hoya Paranoia is quietly accumulating the picks nobody counts.

4wk.verdict: Two fourth-round picks for one. The 2026 fourths have been spent, nothing drafted out of any of it has started a game, and the 2027 fourth remains the only live asset in the deal. That is the usual fate of a fourth-rounder in a twelve-team league.

initial.verdict: A 2027 third for two 2026 fourths. Trade Calculator Guy got volume; Somewhat Goodfellas got the better single asset.

4wk.verdict: A 2027 third against two 2026 fourths. The fourths have been used and produced nothing; the third is still outstanding. Somewhat Goodfellas therefore holds the only thing in this trade that can still become a player.

initial.verdict: Kyren Williams and two picks for Marvin Harrison and a depth back. Both sides solved a real problem, which is the mark of a fair trade and a boring one.

4wk.verdict: Kyren Williams has delivered 71.30 points above replacement in five starts and 16.60 on Sunday, and COME AND TAKE IT took two picks alongside him. Chasing Glory has started neither man it received and no longer owns Marvin Harrison. One of the most one-sided outcomes in this release.

initial.verdict: A pick moved and then moved straight back the next day. Filed here for completeness.

4wk.verdict: Only one side of this has anything in it: a 2026 third to Too High Safeties, with nothing recorded against it. The pick has been spent and nothing from it has started a game, so the asymmetry has cost nobody anything yet.

initial.verdict: The other half of the same 24-hour round trip. Somebody changed their mind.

4wk.verdict: A 2026 third to Not F*cking Around Crew with nothing recorded going back the other way. The pick has been used and has produced no starting points, which makes this a transfer rather than a trade.

initial.verdict: Aaron Jones and two BADS picks for Brian Thomas and Pat Bryant. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. took the older production and the draft capital; Hoya Paranoia took the 23-year-old.

4wk.verdict: Aaron Jones has produced 37.40 above replacement across four starts for Out. Of. Town. Shooters., and a 2026 first and third came with him. Brian Thomas has not started for Hoya Paranoia. Four weeks on, this is the clearest win of the Shooters' pre-season and he has since spent most of what it bought him.

initial.verdict: A 2026 third for a rookie receiver. Fine on both ends and forgettable by November.

4wk.verdict: A third-round pick for a rookie receiver who has not played. Nothing has started for either roster and the pick is already spent, so both halves of this are currently worth zero.

initial.verdict: A 2026 second for Greg Dulcich and a 2027 third. 100 Yards And Runnin turned a tight end nobody wanted into a real pick.

4wk.verdict: Greg Dulcich has started once for Cheddar Bobs and come in 6.10 below replacement, which explains that tight end room better than any other line in this file. 100 Yards And Runnin took a 2026 second and has produced no starts from it.

initial.verdict: A 2026 second for two future thirds. Reasonable rate; nothing here changes a season.

4wk.verdict: A 2026 second against two future third-rounders. Nothing on either side has produced a start. Hoya Paranoia keeps the optionality and 100 Yards And Runnin has already spent its half of the deal.

initial.verdict: Hoya Paranoia buys two 2027 thirds with a 2026 second. He does this constantly and it keeps working.

4wk.verdict: Two 2027 thirds for a 2026 second. The second has been used without producing a start and the thirds are a draft away from existing. Nobody can be graded on this until next April.

initial.verdict: Wan'Dale Robinson and Elijah Arroyo for a 2026 first and a 2027 third. Two teams with opposite timelines both got what they wanted.

4wk.verdict: Wan'Dale Robinson has made three starts for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and returned 3.60 above replacement, 8.30 of it on Sunday. 100 Yards And Runnin took back its own 2026 first and a 2027 third and has produced nothing from either so far.

initial.verdict: Chasing Glory turned Jake Ferguson and two seconds into Tyler Warren, who scored 10.3 in Week 1 and is 24. The best tight-end swap of the offseason.

4wk.verdict: Tyler Warren has started all five weeks for Chasing Glory, returned 20.20 above replacement and scored 21.40 on Sunday. Jake Ferguson has started three times for Trade Calculator Guy and sits 11.50 below replacement, with two second-round picks that have produced nothing travelling alongside him.

initial.verdict: A 2026 first for a 2026 second and a 2027 second. Not F*cking Around Crew is doing the thing that the youngest roster in the league should be doing.

4wk.verdict: A 2026 first for a 2026 second and a 2027 second. Both of the 2026 picks are spent and neither has produced a start. Lovely Day's 2027 second, still sitting with Too High Safeties, is the one live asset left in the trade.

initial.verdict: Chris Godwin for Tre' Harris. Godwin went for 6.3 in Week 1, Harris for 3.5. Nobody won yet.

4wk.verdict: A receiver for a receiver and both of them under water: Chris Godwin 2.90 below replacement in three starts, Tre' Harris 3.20 below in four. Nobody beat the waiver wire, which the model files as no gain rather than as a narrow victory for whoever lost less.

initial.verdict: Tutu Atwell and a 2026 third for a 2028 second. Lovely Day paid a real future pick for a receiver he has never started.

4wk.verdict: A 2028 second against a receiver and a 2026 third. Tutu Atwell has not started for Lovely Day and the third is spent. The only thing in this deal that can still move is the 2028 pick, which belongs to 100 Yards And Runnin.

initial.verdict: Michael Pittman for a 2026 third and a 2028 second. Lovely Day started Pittman in Week 1 for 7.3, which is roughly what this trade is worth.

4wk.verdict: Michael Pittman has started once for Lovely Day and finished 0.50 above replacement. 100 Yards And Runnin collected a 2026 third and a 2028 second for him and is the only side with anything still to come.

initial.verdict: DK Metcalf for Rashid Shaheed and two picks. Metcalf then changed hands again three months later, which tells you what the market thought.

4wk.verdict: Neither roster has started anybody it received, and DK Metcalf has moved on again since — he started for Blame spanos on Sunday for 3.80. The two 2026 picks that travelled with him have produced nothing for Chasing Glory.

initial.verdict: Tee Higgins and Rashid Shaheed for Xavier Worthy, Jalen McMillan, Jordan James and a first. The biggest pure-receiver swap of the offseason, and defensible from both chairs.

4wk.verdict: Tee Higgins has started all five weeks for COME AND TAKE IT and returned 29.60 above replacement. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. took three bodies and a first-round pick and has started none of them. Quantity for quality, four weeks on, with exactly the result the valuation desk keeps predicting.

initial.verdict: Drake London for Brian Thomas and picks. Both are 24-year-old No. 1 receivers; this is two managers trading the same asset with different names.

4wk.verdict: Drake London has started every week for Not F*cking Around Crew and produced 32.50 above replacement, 17.30 of it on Sunday. Brian Thomas has not started for Out. Of. Town. Shooters., which holds a 2027 third and a 2026 first against him and nothing to show for either.

initial.verdict: A five-piece exchange built around Marvin Harrison going one way and Drake London the other. The kind of trade only these two would make.

4wk.verdict: 30.70 points above replacement in five starts for COME AND TAKE IT, and the best player in the deal — Drake London — went to Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and was moved on before he could start a game there. That is the pattern of the Shooters' pre-season in one line: he kept acquiring the right players and selling them inside the week.

initial.verdict: Tee Higgins for Wan'Dale Robinson and a 2026 second. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. got the clearly better player and then traded him again six weeks later.

4wk.verdict: Both men were traded on again before either started for the roster that acquired him. Tee Higgins has started five times this season and none of them was here. Nothing accrues to either side.

initial.verdict: A 2026 second for Jacoby Brissett. A backup quarterback is worth something in superflex — not a second.

4wk.verdict: Jacoby Brissett started for the first time on Sunday and scored 27.78, which the model files as 14.80 above replacement from a single appearance. COME AND TAKE IT has a spent 2026 second to show for it. The cheapest useful quarterback acquisition in this release.

initial.verdict: Derek Carr for nothing recorded. Roster cleanup.

4wk.verdict: Derek Carr has not started for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and nothing at all is recorded going the other way. No production on either side and no pick outstanding, so this one is settled as a blank.

initial.verdict: Marvin Harrison and a 2026 first for Michael Pittman, Malik Willis and a 2028 third. Youth for floor, at a fair rate.

4wk.verdict: Marvin Harrison has not started for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and has changed rosters twice more since. 100 Yards And Runnin's half produced 0.50 above replacement from one start, plus a 2028 third that is still outstanding and is now the deciding asset.

initial.verdict: Not F*cking Around Crew turned Jonathon Brooks and a 2026 first into seven picks. Seven. That is the entire rebuild in one transaction, and the reason the Crew's 2027 draft is going to take a full evening.

4wk.verdict: The deal that built the drawer: seven 2027 selections — four seconds and three thirds — to Not F*cking Around Crew for Jonathon Brooks, a 2026 first and a 2028 third. Brooks has not started for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. and not one of the seven picks exists yet. This cannot be settled before April 2027 and it is the most consequential unsettled trade in the league.

initial.verdict: RJ Harvey and Isaac TeSlaa for two 2026 seconds and change. Harvey is on Lovely Day's roster and Lovely Day started an empty slot instead of him in Week 1, which is its own review.

4wk.verdict: RJ Harvey has made three starts for Lovely Day and returned 22.70 above replacement, though only 0.70 of it arrived on Sunday. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. took three picks, two of them already spent, and holds a 2027 third belonging to a team that is 0-5 — which is the best thing in this trade and will not be collectable until April.

initial.verdict: Joe Mixon for a 2027 third. A 30-year-old running back for a real pick.

4wk.verdict: Joe Mixon has not started for Lovely Day and has since left the roster entirely. 100 Yards And Runnin holds a 2027 third. One side has an asset and the other has a name that no longer appears anywhere in the file.

initial.verdict: Tank Dell and two picks for Xavier Worthy. COME AND TAKE IT got the healthy 23-year-old; Chasing Glory got a receiver who has not been right in two years.

4wk.verdict: Tank Dell has not started for Chasing Glory and Xavier Worthy did not start for COME AND TAKE IT before being moved on again. Two picks travelled with Dell and have produced nothing. A trade between two playoff contenders that has so far changed neither of them.

initial.verdict: Bryce Young and Pat Freiermuth for Daniel Jones and Oronde Gadsden. Young scored 36.44 in Week 1 and Jones 10.04. Early, but the gap is loud.

4wk.verdict: 51.90 above replacement across four starts for Out. Of. Town. Shooters., almost all of it Bryce Young, plus a 2027 second. Lovely Day's side sits 14.40 below replacement across five starts, the worst return attached to any trade in this book, and Daniel Jones gave him 11.08 on Sunday out of the eleventh-ranked quarterback room in the league.

initial.verdict: A.J. Brown for Jalen McMillan and two picks. Lovely Day sold high on a 29-year-old and has since sold him again.

4wk.verdict: A.J. Brown never started for Lovely Day and was traded back to COME AND TAKE IT within a month; Jalen McMillan has not started either. Two picks are spent, nothing has been produced, and the two men involved have since swapped rosters a second time.

initial.verdict: Five young running backs and Josh Downs to Lovely Day for two 2026 seconds and change. Croskey-Merritt started Week 1 and scored 12.1; the shape of this one gets clearer every week.

4wk.verdict: Five bodies to Lovely Day for two and three picks, and the five have made ten starts between them for 14.50 above replacement — Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored 14.20 on Sunday and Josh Downs 6.20. 100 Yards And Runnin's pair have managed one start at 1.30 below replacement. The quantity side won this one, which is rare enough to be worth writing down.

initial.verdict: Rico Dowdle, Chuba Hubbard and Kyle Williams for Marvin Harrison and a fourth. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. bought three startable backs with one receiver he never intended to keep.

4wk.verdict: 30.90 above replacement across four starts for Out. Of. Town. Shooters., and it then sold Chuba Hubbard onward for a 2029 first and $40 a fortnight ago, which makes this the one pre-season deal he has compounded rather than squandered. Marvin Harrison has not started for 100 Yards And Runnin and is on a third roster now.

initial.verdict: Garrett Wilson and a 2026 second for Michael Pittman and Marvin Harrison. COME AND TAKE IT got the best player in the deal and a pick.

4wk.verdict: Garrett Wilson has started every week for COME AND TAKE IT, produced 40.60 above replacement and scored 21.90 on Sunday, with a 2026 second alongside him. Neither man Out. Of. Town. Shooters. received has started for it. The second-biggest margin in this release.

initial.verdict: Malik Willis for a 2026 first. Somewhat Goodfellas paid a first-round pick for a backup quarterback, which superflex explains but does not justify.

4wk.verdict: A 2026 first-round pick for Malik Willis, who has not started for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. Somewhat Goodfellas used the pick and has produced nothing from it yet, which still leaves him holding the better half of a trade that has returned nothing to anybody.

initial.verdict: A first, two seconds and a third change hands with no players involved. Two rebuilders shuffling the same deck.

4wk.verdict: Blame spanos' 2027 first went to Not F*cking Around Crew here, and it is the reason he cannot buy a tight end this week with anything but a player. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. took two 2027 seconds and a 2026 first for passing it along and has produced nothing from the first. Nothing in this settles before April 2027.

retro.verdict: The worst trade in Cartel history, and it happened on startup-draft night. Chasing Glory sent Jared Goff and three picks for Mark Andrews and a second. Goff has started 42 games for Cheddar Bobs and scored 828.5. Andrews started ten, produced 112.9, and was gone. Nothing since has come close.

The cleanest stars-for-picks trade the league has run. Blame spanos gave up five picks — a 2025 first, a 2026 first, a 2026 second and two more — for CeeDee Lamb, who has now started 29 games for him and produced 410.3. 100 Yards And Runnin turned that haul into the deepest roster in the league and still has not reached a final. Both sides got what they were buying; only one of them has a trophy to show for it, and neither does.

COME AND TAKE IT traded Patrick Mahomes and Jakobi Meyers for Tua Tagovailoa, Justin Jefferson and two picks — and then started Jefferson five times before moving him again. Mahomes has started 33 games for Too High Safeties and scored 634.4. The receiving team in this deal is 9-33 lifetime, which tells you how little one great trade fixes.

igross sold Saquon Barkley for Terry McLaurin and Zamir White. Barkley has started 33 games for Hoya Paranoia and produced 597.1 on the way to two titles. McLaurin gave Trade Calculator Guy 261.9 and White gave him 7.0 in two starts. This is how a dynasty gets built and how one doesn't.

Trevor Lawrence for Javonte Williams, Dorian Thompson-Robinson and a 2024 first. Lawrence started 21 games for Blame spanos and scored 439.7. Williams started two and produced 17.1 before being moved. The first-round pick was real value, but in superflex a starting quarterback at that price is a bargain that does not come around often.

Three running backs and a 2026 third for Josh Jacobs. Zack Moss, Rasheen Ali and Audric Estime combined for four points and one start between them. Jacobs has started 25 games for 100 Yards And Runnin and produced 439.1, and is still on the roster. This is the single most lopsided in-season trade in the record.

DK Metcalf and a 2025 first for Garrett Wilson, made on startup night. Metcalf started 31 games for Blame spanos and scored 366.5. Wilson started four for the other side, produced 36.6 and was traded on. The pick going back made this defensible at the time; the production has not been close since.

Jonathan Mingo for De'Von Achane, made on startup night. Achane produced 121.9 in eight starts. Mingo never started a game. Mingo was also Lovely Day's own 1.11 pick in that same draft, which makes this one of the more instructive nights in league history.

Travis Kelce, Calvin Ridley and Josh Jacobs for David Njoku, Anthony Richardson and Zach Charbonnet, in the first week of the league's existence. The Kelce-and-Jacobs side produced 485.9; the other produced 201.8. It is the trade that made the 2023 season and the owner who won it is no longer in the league.

The most evenly matched trade in the record book. Garrett Wilson, Isaiah Likely and Jimmy Garoppolo for Brock Purdy and Sam Darnold: 446.0 against 469.4, a difference of 23 points across three seasons. Wilson started 33 games for Chasing Glory. Purdy started 17 on the other side. Nobody lost this and nobody has stopped arguing about it.

Travis Kelce, Calvin Ridley and Tony Pollard for Alec Pierce and Rashee Rice, at the 2024 deadline. Trade Calculator Guy got 326.5 out of it and a run to the final. Blame spanos got 159.7, mostly from Rice, and Pierce started once.

Daniel Jones for Tua Tagovailoa, which reads like a coin flip and was not. Jones produced 309.3 in 18 starts for COME AND TAKE IT; Tagovailoa gave Blame spanos 147.3 in ten. In superflex the second quarterback slot decides more weeks than anybody admits.

Deebo Samuel for Romeo Doubs and Khalil Shakir. Samuel started 26 games for Hoya Paranoia and produced 263.4 on a championship roster. Doubs and Shakir combined for 83.1 and eight starts. Hoya Paranoia's record in this column is starting to look less like luck.

initial.verdict: Lovely Day sent Drew Lock, a 2028 third and a 2028 fourth to 100 Yards And Runnin for MarShawn Lloyd and Case Keenum. Production is 0.00 on both sides at this gate. On Sunday he started RJ Harvey, a running back, in the superflex slot for the second week running, and the Week 5 lineup filed on Tuesday does it again. The structural hole is the same size and two 2028 picks have left the building. 100 Yards And Runnin adds a fourth quarterback behind Josh Allen and Sam Darnold for nothing he was using, picks up two picks, and keeps a tight end room that leads the league — a straightforward profit for a 2-2 team with the worst luck in the league. initial.verdict: Patrick Mahomes for Cheddar Bobs’ 2027 first, two 2027 seconds and two 2029 fourths. The valuation desk prices the player at 2.62 points per week above replacement and the five picks at 2.62, which is as close to a market-rate trade as this league has produced. The Crew gets the better quarterback in a format that starts two; Too High Safeties gets the first-round pick of a 6-1 team and two seconds from teams that are 1-6 and 2-5, which are the two best seconds in that round. Aaron Rodgers, Rhamondre Stevenson, Aaron Jones and Jacoby Brissett to 100 Yards And Runnin for four 2028 picks. Paying a rounding error for a player priced at nothing is not a disaster, but Lovely Day is twelfth on the dynasty board and 0.2 per cent to make the playoffs, so the direction is wrong on principle. He scored 6.40 in Week 7 — for the team that sold him, under the platform’s lineup lock.

Hunter Henry and a 2029 fourth to Cheddar Bobs for COME AND TAKE IT’s 2027 third and a 2028 fourth. The desk has Henry at 0.97 and the picks going back at 0.17. This paper has been asking Cheddar Bobs to buy a tight end since Week 4, and he has bought one for almost nothing, which is the right way to answer the question. It does not close it: his tight ends have scored 47.8 points in seven weeks, last in the league, and Henry’s 14.10 on Sunday was filed in somebody else’s lineup.

Bryce Young to Too High Safeties for its own 2029 second, the Shooters’ 2027 third returning and the 2027 seconds of 100 Yards And Runnin and Lovely Day. The desk prices Young at 2.26 and the four picks at 1.42, a 23 per cent gap toward the buyer. The context is the part that justifies it: with Mahomes sold on Saturday the roster’s starting quarterback was Gardner Minshew, who scored 0.00 the next afternoon. You can argue about whether Bryce Young is the answer. There was undeniably a question.

Parker Washington to Not F*cking Around Crew for the Crew’s own 2027 first, its own 2027 second and COME AND TAKE IT’s 2027 second. The desk prices Washington at 1.15 and the three picks at 2.62 — 39 per cent lopsided, past the point where this paper will print a proposed trade as a sensible one. It is the same 2.62 the Crew paid for Mahomes forty hours earlier. Washington scored 0.00 in Week 7 and is not in the Week 8 lineup. The Crew is first on the dynasty board and this is how a lead gets spent.

Jaylen Waddle to Hoya Paranoia for Caleb Douglas and Mac Jones. The desk has Waddle at 0.99 against 0.90 for the pair, which is about as level as a two-for-one gets. Hoya Paranoia wanted a starter and started him for 6.80; the Shooters wanted a 23-year-old receiver and got one who put up 20.00 on their bench the same afternoon. Both teams did what their records say they should.

100 Yards And Runnin gets D’Andre Swift, 27, and Darren Waller, 34, for Jordan Watkins and its own 2027 first. On the desk’s Week 4 table that is 2.41 of priced value against 1.52, a 23 percent tilt to the buyer — Waller and Watkins are both unpriced, one for age and one for inexperience. The football case is sound: Swift walks into the tenth-best backfield in the league on a roster that is first at tight end and third at receiver. The cost is the hedge. A 4-4 team with the worst luck figure in the Cartel has sold the one asset that gets more valuable if the season goes wrong. Lovely Day, 3-5 and last on the dynasty board, took a first-round pick for two men he could not win with, which is the right trade for his position and a better one if the buyer is wrong.

Raptor sends Kimani Vidal and takes Ray Davis back, the first of two moves he made inside six hours on Wednesday night. Neither man is priced above 0.31 on the desk's Week 4 table and neither started in Week 9 — Davis scored 0.20 on a bench, Vidal 4.10 on another. What makes it a B rather than a shrug is the shape: Chasing Glory is tenth of twelve at receiver with 230.10 points while leading the league at quarterback and running back, and he spent the evening buying at the position he is short in rather than the ones he is deep in. igross, at 0.1 percent with $199 he cannot spend, took back a 25-year-old for a 26-year-old and nothing else. That is not a mistake. It is also not a plan.

Six hours after the first deal, Raptor sent Joe Milton to Too High Safeties for Tre Tucker, and both managers started the man they had just acquired. Tucker took a Week 9 receiver slot and returned 7.50. Milton went into the superflex and returned 13.16, which beat four of the other eleven superflex slots in the league and was the third-best score on an 0-9 roster that converted 94.9 percent of itself and still lost by 3.14. Tucker is priced at 0.31 and Milton is not priced at all, so the table has nothing to say about this. The lineup cards did: two clubs identified a hole, filled it on a Wednesday night and were both better for it on the Sunday. The grades are for the process.
